title: From Summer Intern to Head of US Sustainability: How JBS's Management Trainee Program Shaped One Career
summary: This profile is the first in a series spotlighting graduates of the JBS Management Trainee Program and the careers they've built across our business.
body_markdown:
*This profile is the first in a series spotlighting graduates of the JBS Management Trainee Program and the careers they've built across our business. Through their stories, we're sharing how JBS invests in developing talent and opening doors for the next generation of agricultural leaders.*


**Article Summary:**


- JBS’s Management Trainee Program helps new graduates grow into leadership roles.
- Program trainees rotate across the business to find a mutual best fit.
- Trainees reconvene every six months for dedicated leadership development.
- Participants gain early ownership, executive access, and a lasting peer network.
- Madison Boyd joined JBS as a summer intern in 2016 and became a management trainee in 2017.
- Madison now serves as Head of Sustainability for JBS USA and leads ESG and GHG reporting globally nearly a decade later.


When Madison Boyd arrived at Mississippi State University in 2013, she planned to become a large-animal veterinarian. Having grown up in Washington, D.C. with parents who worked on agricultural issues in government, she also had long been passionate about advocacy in the food and agriculture industries.


Near the end of her junior year, JBS was recruiting on Madison’s campus. Speaking with a recruiter ultimately led her somewhere she hadn't expected: a decade-long career in sustainability.


Today, Madison holds a dual role as Head of Sustainability for JBS USA and leads Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) and Greenhouse Gas (GHG) reporting, overseeing the company's global non-financial disclosure.


### Learning the business from the inside out


Midway through her internship, Madison learned about the JBS Management Trainee Program. One feature in particular stood out about the program: the chance to rotate through different functions within the company and find the mutual best fit. Before entering her senior year, she was accepted into the program to start after graduation – and she’s never looked back.


Her first project as a Management Trainee was helping write JBS USA's first-ever sustainability report, an assignment that required her to understand every department and every business unit.


"That was an incredible way to learn about the company," she said. "It's absolutely to credit for where I am today and how I now oversee all of our global ESG reporting. I wouldn't have gotten that opportunity at other companies at 21 years old."


For Madison, the defining quality of the program was the ownership it handed to young employees, along with the room to grow.


"You get a lot of ownership early on," she said. "You are essentially given a license to try different things and to prove your worth. That resonated with me a lot."


### A company built on values


Madison was also impressed with how JBS genuinely lived its values. Interns heard directly and often from executive leaders, whose talks regularly centered on the company's principles.


"It was the first time I'd been exposed to a company where the values were more than words on a wall," she said. "These executives were very busy, and it didn't seem like they were following a script. It was embedded in their day-to-day. There was a lot of integrity in that."


### Relationships that last


For a shared services function like sustainability, which depends on relationships across the entire business, the internal network Madison built as a trainee proved just as valuable as the technical knowledge.


Her fellow trainees went on to become plant environmental heads, HR directors, and leaders across every business unit, colleagues she still calls upon today.


### Advice for prospective JBS Management Trainees


Having recently spoken with undergraduates entering the workforce, Madison keeps her advice simple.


"Do it," she said. "It's a great way to start your career and get exposure to career paths you didn't know existed, in a field you're passionate about."


The rest, she believes, comes down to effort and two values she still carries with her: humility and ownership.


Madison said she received that same advice from JBS’ Head of Human Resources, and it continues to guide her today.


“She told me, ‘If you show up, listen, stay humble, and find ways to add value, we can train the rest. From there, the sky's the limit.’”


### Start your own story with JBS


Madison's path is just one of many that begin with the JBS Management Trainee Program. Designed to help new graduates build the skills, relationships, and real-world experience needed to grow into leadership roles, the program is a launchpad for careers across our business.
